stem: A simulation predicts success on a 30° slope, but the real robot flips under the same intended test conditions. What can be concluded?
topic: Python as Modelling and Simulation Tool

citations.evidenceText:
Modelling and Simulation - Verification and Validation
 –  Verification: "Was the model built correctly?".
      •    It determines if the simulation code accurately reflects the conceptual model and
         specifications.
      •   This involves checking the software code. In robotics, this means ensuring that the
       C++ or Python control algorithms correctly implement the intended mathematical
        kinematic equations without bugs
–   Validation: "Was the right model built?".
      •    It measures how well the model matches reality within the context of its intended
        use. Techniques range from informal reviews to formal logical proofs.
      •   This measures how well the simulated robot matches the
         physical robot's performance in the real world. If the
        simulated robot can climb a 30-degree slope but the real
        robot flips over, the model is invalid.
      •   Validation prevents false confidence in simulation outcomes.

solution.justification: A bare line ending after the binary operator is not a complete statement outside an enclosing continuation context.

optionExplanations.o1: Correct. A bare line ending after the binary operator is not a complete statement outside an enclosing continuation context.
optionExplanations.o2: Incorrect. No such implicit continuation is present in the printed snippet.
optionExplanations.o3: Incorrect. Adjacency is insufficient here; an explicit syntactic continuation is needed.
optionExplanations.o4: Incorrect. Parsing fails rather than choosing an alternative divisor.
